note: Original greeting lines for Harbour Bend (fictional). All lines are plain English for now. Lines in Nigerian Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo or Hausa should be written or reviewed by a native-speaking writer before they are added, and marked "reviewed": true.

trader.text: Good afternoon! Fresh tomatoes and pepper today, come and see.
Welcome, my customer. Take your time, look around.
Market is full today. Everybody is buying for the weekend.
If you want the bus park, it is just across the road.

driver.text: Bus park is busy today. Everybody wants to go somewhere.
Harbour Road is moving slowly. Give yourself extra time.
Good day! I hope your journey goes smoothly.

elder.text: Ah, young man. Walk well, and greet your people for me.
This street has changed a lot since I was your age.
Good evening. Do not stay out too late.

youth.text: Nice day for a walk by the water.
You see the new food spot by the square? The jollof there is serious.
Careful on that bridge, they still have not finished fixing it.

mechanic.text: Bring the car into the bay and I will look at it.
Every knock on the road ends up in my workshop. Drive gently.
New paint? I have colours. Bring money.

startled.text: Do you want to knock somebody down?

tailor.text: Come in, let me see your size.
This fabric just arrived. The colours are beautiful.
A good outfit changes how people greet you.

attendant.text: Pump is working today, thank God.
Everybody is buying diesel this week.
Mind the pumps when you drive in.

rival.text: You again? Your car is too slow for this island.
The boulevard is mine on race day.
Respect. Not everybody can keep up with me.

office.text: Meetings all day. I just came down for fresh air.
The towers' generator ran all night.
Good afternoon. Busy day on the island.

range.text: Eyes forward, finger off the trigger until you're on the line.
Range Day is open. Beat the clock and earn a medal.
Breathe out, then squeeze. Don't pull.

armourer.text: Medals from Coach Kola open up more of my stock.
Rounds, armour, everything is on the counter.
Keep it on the range, or the patrol will come asking.
